newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian president launches talks after PM quits.
newsitem.headline: Latvian president launches talks after PM quits.

text.p: Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis on Tuesday began talks with political parties on the resignation of Prime Minister Andris Shkele, who quit amid a row with the president over a new finance minister.

Shkele quit after Ulmanis called on parliament to reject the premier's choice for finance minister, Vassily Melnik, after reports Melnik had been investigated by prosecutors under anti-corruption laws.
The resignation has shocked Latvia where Shkele was seen as a lynchpin in efforts to accelerate economic reforms launched after the small country quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
"The state president has begun consultations with political parties and parliamentary factions," the president's office said in a statement. It did not say how long the talks would last.
A spokeswoman for the president said Ulmanis would talk to the political parties to decide whether to ask Shkele to continue as prime minister or name a new head of government.
The president's office said that during a meeting between Ulmanis and Shkele late on Monday all "misunderstandings were smoothed out and contradictions clarified".
The row over Melnik erupted after a newspaper reported he had been invesigated by the prosecutor's office for a conflict of interest by holding state and private posts at the same time.
The prosecutor's office confirmed it had investigated Melnik and had found no wrong-doing. Melnik was voted into office by parliament despite the president's plea.
Shkele came into power at the end of 1995 and stressed that his main task would be to improve the country's finances after a damaging banking crisis earlier that year.
He leads an eight-party coalition but has managed to keep the government together despite internal bickering.
He has said his key achivement is the passing of the country's first balanced budget but he has also helped to speed privatisation and make Latvia more investor-friendly.
